function: Joint channel estimation and data detection for MIMO-OFDM with superimposed pilots; a learned flow model is the channel prior, symbols updated analytically (p. 2, p. 5-6).
system: MIMO-OFDM, 4 transmit and 4 receive antennas, 3.5 GHz, 48 subcarriers, 12 symbols per frame; superimposed pilots (data power 0.9, pilot 0.1); no RIS (p. 8-9).
method: Unsupervised conditional flow matching: U-Net velocity field trained offline on unlabeled channels as prior; predictor-corrector ODE inference with likelihood correction; analytic Tweedie symbol update (p. 6-9).
data_channel: 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL, 3.5 GHz, 300 ns delay spread, 3 km/h; trained on CDL-C in the shift test; 8000 training samples, 8:1:1 split (p. 8-9, p. 12-13).
test_conditions: Train on CDL-C; test on CDL-C and unseen CDL-A, CDL-B; same CFM-Rx for QPSK, 8-PSK, 16-PSK data; SNR -10 to 20 dB (p. 8, p. 12).
baselines: Non-learned: 5G-NR LMMSE estimation and equalization (oracle and practical covariance), LS. Learned: DM-JED diffusion receiver, E2E supervised CNN; CFM-TEQ ablation (p. 9-11).
metrics: Channel estimation NMSE, uncoded BER, throughput, BER versus sampling steps, FLOPs, parameters (p. 9-13).
complexity: Inference complexity O(T k^2 Cmax^2 NS NT), T = 30; 1.014×10^5 parameters, 5.705×10^7 FLOPs versus DM-JED 8.942×10^7 and E2E 7.596×10^8 FLOPs (p. 12-13).
openness: Code at https://github.com/fhghwericge/CFMRx-for-MIMO-Receiver-Design-with-Superimposed-Pilots (p. 2); channel data simulated, no dataset link.
q1_support: p. 8: "based on the 3GPP clustered delay line (CDL) channel model, as specified in TR 38.901"
q2_support: p. 12: "we train all models on the CDL-C channel model and evaluate them on two other unseen channel models, namely CDL-A and CDL-B"
q3_support: p. 9: "5G-NR: A modular receiver using LMMSE channel estimation followed by LMMSE equalization" (non-learned) and "DM-JED: A state-of-the-art diffusion model for joint channel estimation and data detection [9]" (learned); NMSE and BER compared on p. 9-10.
q4_support: p. 13: "In terms of computational complexity, CFM-Rx demands just" 5.705×10^7 FLOPs and 1.014×10^5 parameters (Table 1); the complexity order is on p. 12.
q5_support: p. 2: "The source code is available at: https://github.com/fhghwericge/CFMRx-for-MIMO-Receiver-Design-with-Superimposed-Pilots"
notes: Include, area 1: joint estimation and detection, and BER and throughput carry most results (Figs. 5-9, 11-12) while NMSE appears once (Fig. 4, p. 9), so area 2 is the alternative. Only the channel prior is learned; symbols are updated analytically (p. 5). GitHub link not opened.
